basis: Congenital neutrophil deficiency impairs immunity; oral ulceration and periodontal damage occur in 30-79%. Recurrent infections are secondary diseases.
Bordetella pertussis infection directly affects respiratory epithelium.
LAMC2-related junctional skin fragility; enamel hypoplasia is characteristic of junctional EB and common (>30%), although subtype-specific data are sparse.
Rabies virus causes encephalomyelitis. Salivation, gastrointestinal symptoms and centrally mediated vocal cord paresis do not establish additional organ injury.
Inherited progesterone receptor resistance is an endocrine hormone-response disorder; associated infertility adds no organ axis.
Structural stenosis of the heart's pulmonary valve; the pulmonary name does not indicate lung disease.
Chronic bilirubin brain injury; auditory neuropathy/hearing loss occurs in 30-99%. Dental enamel dysplasia is a classic diagnostic feature; jaundice does not establish liver injury.
Palmar and plantar skin toxicity defines the condition. Tingling alone does not establish peripheral nerve damage.
Lysosomal storage disease with progressive neurodegeneration; skeletal dysplasia is common (~30% or more). Optic damage varies; hepatomegaly alone does not establish dysfunction.
Familial atrophic, varioliform skin scars define this disorder; macular atrophy here refers to skin lesions, not retinal disease.
Neoplasm arises in or occupies a cerebral hemisphere.
Maternal anti-Kell antibodies cause fetal/neonatal erythroid suppression and hemolytic anemia; alloimmune blood-cell disease.
Skin and dental dysplasia define IP. Ocular abnormalities include frequent corneal opacity and strabismus (~55%); neurologic involvement is near 30%, with frequent seizures annotated.
Gastric mucosal inflammation and subepithelial collagen deposition define the disease; an autoimmune mechanism is not established.
Structural myocardial non-compaction affects the heart; skeletal muscle involvement is not established across this concept.
Carcinoma confined to the ureter, which belongs to the renal axis.
Inherited platelet and erythroid abnormalities, sometimes with neutropenia; no additional organ injury is characteristic across the group.
Familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is a disease of cardiac myocardium.
Umbrella for disorders arising from HIV-associated immunodeficiency; no single anatomical organ is consistently affected across its subtypes.
Developmental disability and skeletal/digital anomalies define the syndrome. Hearing impairment occurs in 4/13 (~31%); feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal injury.
Primary ovarian insufficiency causes loss of gonadal endocrine function; infertility and amenorrhea add no further axis.
Immune-mediated motor peripheral neuropathy with conduction block. Muscle weakness reflects denervation rather than a primary muscle disease.
Calcium oxalate stones affect the urinary tract; stone composition and inheritance alone do not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Umbrella for skeletal muscle disorders causing myotonia. Cardiac, endocrine and other manifestations are subtype-specific.
Isolated cleft lip and/or palate is a structural disorder of the mouth.
